## Upstream changes 8.9.1 -> 9.0.0

**Verdict:** DO NOT APPLY UNATTENDED — the notes require MongoDB `8.0` ("### Engine versions - MongoDB: `8.0`"), but the compose file pins `mongodb: &mongodb-image ${ROCKETCHAT_MONGODB_IMAGE_TAG:-mongo:${ROCKETCHAT_MONGODB_IMAGE_VERSION:-7.0@sha256:...}}`. This requirement is new at this version — the 8.9.1 baseline notes list MongoDB `8.0` too, so it is *not* newly introduced by this range (it already applied at 8.9.1, see Data and dependencies), but the compose file's actual pin of 7.0 means Rocket.Chat 9.0.0 would run on an engine version its own release notes never certify. Also several authentication methods break on upgrade unless action is taken first.

### Breaking changes
- LDAP, SAML and Custom OAuth become Premium-only: `"Makes LDAP and SAML authentication Premium features. **Breaking:** workspaces without a Premium plan that includes the `ldap-enterprise` or `saml-enterprise` module lose LDAP and SAML login on upgrade to 9.0.0."` and `"Makes Custom OAuth authentication a Premium feature... the enable setting of every Custom OAuth service falls back to `false`, Custom OAuth logins are refused..."`
- Built-in Drupal, Facebook, GitHub Enterprise, LinkedIn, Meteor, Twitter, WordPress and Dolphin OAuth login providers are removed: `"Removes the built-in Drupal, Facebook, GitHub Enterprise, LinkedIn, Meteor, Twitter, WordPress and Dolphin OAuth login providers."`
- 157 Meteor/DDP methods removed: `"**Breaking:** Removed 157 Meteor (DDP) methods that no longer have callers inside the Rocket.Chat codebase... External DDP/SDK clients that still invoke these by name will receive a `Method 'X' not found [404]` error."`
- Webhook integration scripts no longer transpiled with Babel, now run in strict-mode V8 (`isolated-vm`): `"**Breaking:** Stopped transpiling webhook integration scripts with Babel. Scripts now run as-is..."` — implicit globals, `this` in nested functions, `arguments.callee`, octal literals and duplicate params all behave differently or throw.
- `phone` user field replaced by `phones` array: `"**Breaking:** the `phone` user field is replaced by the `phones` array (`{ number, label? }[]`); existing numbers are migrated automatically on upgrade."`
- `freeSwitchExtension` renamed to `sipExtension` on users; REST integrations using the old field name break: `"Renames the user `freeSwitchExtension` attribute to `sipExtension`... REST API integrations must switch to the new name..."`
- REST API status codes change for auth/authorization failures (401/403 reshuffled, bodies change shape): `"**Breaking:** REST API status codes for authentication and authorization failures now follow their meaning..."` and the follow-up 403 unification in PR #43214.
- `query`/`fields` REST params and `ALLOW_UNSAFE_QUERY_AND_FIELDS_API_PARAMS` removed: `"Removes the deprecated `query` and `fields` REST API parameters, along with the `ALLOW_UNSAFE_QUERY_AND_FIELDS_API_PARAMS` environment variable that re-enabled them."`
- `/ufs` legacy file download endpoint removed: `"Removes `/ufs` legacy endpoint for downloading files"`
- Anonymous write/login removed, `anonymous` role deleted, affected users deactivated and logged out: `"On upgrade the setting and role are deleted from the database and any existing users holding the `anonymous` role are deactivated and logged out."`
- Atlassian Crowd integration removed; Crowd-provisioned users must switch login method: `"Users previously provisioned through Crowd keep their accounts... but must sign in through another authentication method."`
- WebDAV, Gravatar, legacy federation/Matrix Bridge, legacy GCM push settings all removed and cleared from the database (see respective notes).
- `POST /v1/push.token` response shape flattened: `"Changes the `POST /v1/push.token` response to return flat `tokenValue` and `tokenType` fields instead of the nested `token` object."`
- `/hooks` endpoints change status codes/body shapes on failure (403/404/500 instead of uniform 400).

### Variables
- `MESSAGE_MAX_PARSE_LENGTH` default changes from `0` (unlimited) to `10000`: `"Changes the default value of the `MESSAGE_MAX_PARSE_LENGTH` environment variable from `0` (no limit) to `10000` characters."` Not set in this compose file's environment block or `.env.example`, so the host inherits the new default. Only matters if `Message_MaxAllowedSize` is raised above 5000.
- `ALLOW_UNSAFE_QUERY_AND_FIELDS_API_PARAMS` removed (not referenced in this compose/.env.example, so no action needed here, but any external automation using it will break).
- No variables in this template's compose file or `.env.example` are renamed or newly required by this release.

### Data and dependencies
- Already true at 8.9.1 (not a change introduced by this range): MongoDB `8.0` is required — the 8.9.1 baseline notes already state `"MongoDB: \`8.0\`"`. The compose file pins `mongo:7.0`, so the deployment is already out of line with upstream's stated engine requirement before this upgrade is even applied. This is a standing mismatch, not something 9.0.0 introduces, but it is the reason the verdict cannot be SAFE TO APPLY.
- Node engine requirement unchanged (`>=22.22.3 <23 || >=24.15.0 <25`), and the image itself moves to Node 24.22.1 on Debian bookworm per the summary — this is an image-internal change, not something the compose file controls.
- `phone` → `phones` and `freeSwitchExtension` → `sipExtension` migrate automatically on upgrade (irreversible field rename, done in-place against the live database).
- Unused MongoDB indexes dropped automatically: `"The upgrade drops unused MongoDB indexes"` (irreversible, routine).
- Stale `Drafts` sidebar group migration runs against `Accounts_Default_User_Preferences_sidebarSectionsOrder` and every user's `sidebarCategories` preference.
- Various settings (Crowd, WebDAV, Gravatar, legacy federation/Matrix, legacy GCM push, `Use_RC_SDK`) are deleted from the database on upgrade — not reversible by downgrading the image alone.

### Before applying
- Confirm the compose file's MongoDB pin against what 9.0.0 requires before upgrading Rocket.Chat: either raise `ROCKETCHAT_MONGODB_IMAGE_VERSION` to a `8.0.x` tag (with matching digest) and perform the MongoDB major-version upgrade first, with a verified backup, or do not proceed with the Rocket.Chat image bump yet.
- Confirm at least one admin account can log in with local username/password before upgrading, per the release banner: `"**Before you update:** make sure at least one administrator can log in with a local username and password."`
- If LDAP, SAML or Custom OAuth are in use, confirm an active Premium plan with the relevant module (`ldap-enterprise`, `saml-enterprise`, `oauth-enterprise`), or migrate affected users to local/Google/GitHub/GitLab/Apple/Nextcloud login before upgrading.
- If any users signed in via Drupal, Facebook, GitHub Enterprise, LinkedIn, Meteor, Twitter, WordPress or Dolphin OAuth, notify them to switch to a supported login method — their accounts survive but the login method is removed.
- Audit any external scripts/bots using removed Meteor DDP methods, the `query`/`fields` REST params, `/ufs`, or `ALLOW_UNSAFE_QUERY_AND_FIELDS_API_PARAMS`, and migrate them to the listed REST equivalents beforehand.
- Review any custom webhook integration scripts for sloppy-mode JavaScript (implicit globals, `arguments.callee`, octal literals, duplicate params) that will now throw under strict mode.
- Take a MongoDB backup (the `backups` service in this compose file already runs `mongodump` on a schedule — trigger/verify a fresh one) before upgrading, given the irreversible field renames and index drops.
- After upgrade, re-check any REST API client code that inspects HTTP status codes or `errorType` for auth/authorization failures (401/403 reshuffle).

### Notes read
- RocketChat/Rocket.Chat release notes for `9.0.0` (full detail section, Major/Minor/Patch changes).
- RocketChat/Rocket.Chat release notes for `8.9.1`, supplied as the current-baseline section, used only to confirm which requirements (MongoDB 8.0, Node range) already applied before this upgrade.
